Title: Diagnosis of test `testLang412Right`

Details:
The test `testLang412Right` calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight` on a StrBuilder instance with a `null` argument for the string, a width of 10, and a pad character '*'.

Examining the `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` method, the method first ensures capacity for the new characters. Then it converts the object to a string as follows:
```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
```
Therefore, if `obj` is `null`, the method calls `getNullText()` to get the string to use. 

Next, the method gets the length of this string and either copies it up to the width or pads it with the padChar to the right to make the full specified width.

Examining the `getNullText()` method, it simply returns `nullText`. The problem lies in the value of `nullText`. If `nullText` is also `null`, then the subsequent call `str.length()` in line 1230 will throw a `NullPointerException`.

From the test, since no null text has been set on the StrBuilder instance, `nullText` is presumably `null`. Thus, when the method attempts to calculate the length of `str` (which is `null`), the test fails with a `NullPointerException`.

Therefore, the bug is that when `null` is appended via `appendFixedWidthPadRight`, the default `nullText` has not been initialized and remains `null`, causing a null pointer dereference during length calculation.

Best places to fix this would be in:
- Ensuring a default non-null value for `nullText` upon StrBuilder initialization.
- Alternatively, modifying `appendFixedWidthPadRight` to handle `nullText == null` gracefully by substituting an empty string or a default string.

Recommended methods to fix:

org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(java.lang.Object, int, char)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.getNullText()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
